items.title: Iran's supreme leader killed
items.description: Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei has been killed in Israeli and US strikes, Iran's state-controlled media has reported.

items.title: Iranian strikes damage Dubai airport and luxury hotel
items.description: Iran's retaliatory strikes have damaged Dubai's international airport and the landmark sail-shaped Burj Al Arab hotel.

items.title: Ali Khamenei mastered the art of pitting his enemies against each other
items.description: A conservative Islamic scholar with a head for politics, Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei succeeded his mentor in the wake of the Iran-Iraq War — and consolidated his grip on power over the following decades.

items.title: Australia 'did not participate' in Operation Epic Fury in Iran
items.description: Foreign Minister Penny Wong has confirmed Australia was not involved in the major Israeli-United States operation in Iran that has reportedly decapitated its leadership.

items.title: Travellers stranded as US-Iran conflict throws international flights into disarray
items.description: Nations closing airspace and suspending flights include major international transit hubs connecting Australian travellers with Europe and Asia.

items.title: 'Fill up your car' before petrol price spikes, analyst says

items.title: Joy and grief as Iranian Australians react to US-Israeli airstrikes
items.description: Iranian Australians are attending large gatherings around the country to mark the death of Iran's supreme leader in air strikes by the United States and Israel.

items.title: A Melbourne dad was shot dead in Bali. The accused argue it was a debt 'scare' gone wrong
items.description: Three Australian men are waiting to be sentenced after a months-long trial for the alleged murder of a Melbourne father. Police say it was a deliberate hit job, while the men say it wasn't intentional.

items.title: Canadian backpacker's family calls for coronial inquest after death on K'gari
items.description: The 19-year-old is remembered at a funeral on Vancouver Island as her parents call for an inquest into her death on Queensland's K'gari.

items.title: 'Timing is impeccable': Record rain for parts of SA

items.title: Question about Khamenei's death to Iran's women's football team quickly shutdown
items.description: As the world reacts to the death of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, the Iranian women's football team prepares to play its opening Women's Asian Cup game in Australia.

items.title: Crichton kicks golden-point winner to down Dragons in Vegas
items.description: Canterbury captain Stephen Crichton kicks a field goal to beat the Dragons 15-14 in golden point as the 2026 NRL season kicks off in Las Vegas.

items.title: Inside the search for our next Olympians, eight years out from Brisbane games

items.title: Sienna survived childhood cancer. Then, her heart began to fail
items.description: After overcoming cancer as a child, scans revealed her heart was "working under half of what it should".

items.title: SA Labor pledges to wipe public school fees as Liberals target zero ocean litter
items.description: Labor has vowed to abolish public school fees for primary and high school students from 2027, if it's returned to Government, while the Liberal Party said it will commit $4.3 million to stop stormwater litter reaching South Australia's coastline.

items.title: Too tall, too old, too Aussie: I'm a tough sell for arranged marriage

items.title: Get ready trivia nuts. It's time to play, HARD!

items.title: Some Scream fans are boycotting the new edition. Here’s why
items.description: Weinstein, copycat panic, leaked scripts, closed studios and departing stars — Scream's 30-year journey has been anything but smooth and the seventh edition in the cornerstone slasher series is no different.

items.title: 'Their dirty secrets, not mine': Former prison officers speak out about NSW system
items.description: Current and former NSW prison officers describe what they say is a toxic workplace culture and a system that shields officers accused of serious misconduct, rather than holding them accountable. They argue it has driven younger officers out of the service.

items.title: Seventh narco sub found near Australian waters, signalling 'insane amount of drugs'
items.description: At least seven narco subs have been discovered in Pacific waters near Australia in the past 18 months, with experts warning that Australia's cocaine demand means more are on the way.

items.title: Inpex emissions 'systematically underestimated' since 2018, report finds
items.description: An independent review into oil and gas company Inpex has found widespread and persistent failures in how emissions were calculated, recorded and reported, dating back to the start of production in 2018.

items.title: How university life in Australia has changed
items.description: Two students who went to the same university 30 years apart share their radically different experiences as lectures go online and face-to-face contact takes a back seat in the post-pandemic world.

items.title: Crocodiles spotted in Newcastle creek
items.description: Reptile experts are searching for several juvenile freshwater crocodiles that have been spotted in a New South Wales creek.

items.title: Extreme rhetoric in right-wing political circles deserves more attention

items.title: Your complete guide to the Matildas Women's Asian Cup squad
